question: A beam of continuous white light is passed through a gas and dark lines are observed in the spectrum. Explain why these dark lines are formed.

options.A: White light passing through a gas produces bright emission lines because the gas emits all wavelengths.
options.B: White light contains a continuous range of wavelengths. Gas atoms selectively absorb certain definite wavelengths, which are then missing from transmitted light and appear as dark lines; the result is an absorption line spectrum.
options.C: Dark lines are produced because all wavelengths are scattered equally by the gas.
options.D: The gas converts white light into ultraviolet light, producing dark lines.
